title: findElement
summary: Find matching elements in an htmlTree object.

gpu_support.notes: `findElement` traverses host-resident HTML metadata and does not use provider kernels.

description: `findElement(tree, selector)` searches a RunMat `htmlTree` object and returns matching subtrees as a column cell array of scalar `htmlTree` objects.
behaviors: `tree` must be a scalar RunMat `htmlTree` object or a cell array of `htmlTree` objects.
`selector` must be a string scalar or character vector.
Numeric, logical, complex, and provider-resident inputs are not htmlTree or selector values and reject before any provider access.

Supported selectors include element tags, `*`, `.class`, `#id`, `[attr]`, `[attr=value]`, `[attr~=value]`, `[attr|=value]`, `[attr^=value]`, `[attr$=value]`, `[attr*=value]`, descendant combinators, child combinators (`>`), adjacent-sibling combinators (`+`), general-sibling combinators (`~`), comma-separated groups, `:empty`, `:first-child`, `:first-of-type`, and `:not(...)` for these supported pseudo-classes.

Attribute names are matched case-insensitively through the parser's lowercase attribute map. Attribute values, ids, and classes use CSS-style exact, whitespace-list, dash-prefix, prefix, suffix, or substring string matching according to the selector operator.
Sibling matching follows element siblings and ignores intervening whitespace text nodes.
The result is a column cell array because RunMat does not yet have a first-class MATLAB object-array representation for `htmlTree`.
Unsupported CSS pseudo-classes and selector forms raise an explicit error instead of silently returning partial results.
Full CSS3 selector parity remains tracked by the broader Text Analytics compatibility issue.

examples.output: `lead` is a one-element cell array containing the matching `P` subtree.

examples.input:
tree = htmlTree("
ManualGuide
"); pdfs = findElement(tree, "a[href$='.pdf']")
examples.output: `pdfs` contains the link whose `href` ends with `.pdf`.
`firstLink` contains the first `A` element under the section.

faqs.question: Does `findElement` return a MATLAB object array?
faqs.answer: No. RunMat currently returns a column cell array of scalar `htmlTree` objects because generic object-array identity semantics are still tracked separately.

faqs.question: Does RunMat support every CSS selector accepted by MATLAB?
faqs.answer: No. Common tag, id, class, attribute operator, group, descendant, child, sibling, `:empty`, `:first-child`, `:first-of-type`, and simple `:not(...)` forms are supported. Full CSS3 parity remains tracked in the Text Analytics umbrella issue.

faqs.question: Does `findElement` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It traverses host HTML metadata and has no `runmat-accelerate` provider path.

example.output: `subtrees` is a column cell array of scalar `htmlTree` objects.

points: `tree` must be an `htmlTree` object or a cell array of `htmlTree` objects.
`selector` must use the supported selector subset documented above.

gpu_residency: `findElement` traverses host-resident HTML metadata and has no provider kernel.
